Fit each run's map from minutes onto a library's iRT scale, and convert times either way

library_calibrate_rt.Rd

Fit each run's map from retention time in minutes onto a spectral library's iRT scale from anchors you choose, and convert the times you send with them, in either direction.

Answers where should this library precursor elute in my run? and what is this run's minute on the library's scale? A spectral library stores retention time on a run-independent scale, iRT (Escher et al. 2012); a run reports minutes. mzLib's IrtCalibration.Fit maps one onto the other from anchors: precursors you identified confidently in the run, each with its observed apex time in minutes and its library iRT. The fit is robust: it starts from binned medians and downweights anchors far from the curve (Tukey bisquare), so some wrong identifications do not bend it. It is strictly increasing, so it inverts. By default it is a LOWESS curve (Cleveland 1979) that follows a gradient that bends; kind = "linear" fits one straight line.

Usage

library_calibrate_rt(anchors, queries = NULL, kind = NULL, minimum_anchors = NULL,
  bandwidth = NULL, knots = NULL, robustness_iterations = NULL, on_error = "fail",
  timeout = 60)

Arguments

anchors

One row per anchor: a data.frame with columns group (any name: the run), rt_minutes (the observed retention time, in minutes) and irt (the library's indexed retention time, in iRT), or a list of list(group, rt_minutes, irt). They travel on stdin, one line each. mzLib refuses an NA or NaN time.

queries

Times to convert, in the same shape: each row gives its group and exactly one of rt_minutes (minutes, converted to iRT) or irt (iRT, converted to minutes), the other NA. A data.frame may leave out the column it never gives. Each group's queries use that group's fit. NULL (the default) converts nothing: you get each group's fit and its anchors' residuals.

kind

"linear" or "lowess", mzLib's IrtCalibrationKind. NULL (the default) sends nothing, so mzLib's default, LOWESS, applies.

minimum_anchors

A group with fewer anchors than this is refused, not fitted (anchors). NULL (the default) leaves mzLib's default, 20 anchors at the pin. mzLib requires at least 3.

bandwidth

LOWESS only: the fraction of anchors in each local fit, in (0, 1]. Smaller follows the gradient, and its noise, more closely. NULL (the default) leaves mzLib's default, 0.3.

knots

LOWESS only: how many evenly spaced times between the first and last anchor the curve is fitted at (points); between them it is a straight line. NULL (the default) leaves mzLib's default, 100 points. At least 3.

robustness_iterations

Rounds of Tukey bisquare reweighting after the first fit (iterations). NULL (the default) leaves mzLib's default, 3 iterations. 0 or more.

on_error

"fail" (the default) stops at the first group mzLib refuses, with an mzlib_usage_error naming it; "skip" records the refusal in that group's row of groups and fits the rest. An option mzLib refuses fails the call either way.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

Each group (a run, typically) is fitted on its own anchors, and the queries you send for it are converted with that fit: give a time in minutes to get its iRT, or an iRT to get the minutes at which that precursor should elute in this run.

You choose the anchors. mzLib applies no q-value cutoff, and mzLibR adds none. Send the queries in the same call as their anchors: mzLib keeps the fitted curve's points private, so a calibration cannot be returned and used later. Refitting the same anchors gives the same map, because mzLib sorts them first.

Value

An mzlibr_rt_calibration.

records is a data.frame with one row per anchor, then one per query, in the order sent: group, as sent; role, "anchor", "to_irt" (you gave minutes) or "to_minutes" (you gave iRT); rt_minutes (min), as given, or the converted time for a "to_minutes" query, NA when the group was not fitted and you gave none; irt (iRT), as given, or the converted value for a "to_irt" query, NA likewise; fitted_irt (iRT), anchors only, the curve's iRT at the anchor's time, so irt - fitted_irt is its residual, NA on a query or when the group was not fitted; and is_extrapolated, whether rt_minutes lies outside the group's anchors, where the map is a straight-line continuation rather than a fit, NA when the group was not fitted.

groups is a data.frame, one row per group in order of first appearance: group; kind, the shape mzLib fitted (NA: not fitted); anchor_count, the anchors it was fitted from (anchors; the anchors sent, if refused); query_count, the times converted (queries); residual_sd, how far the anchors that fit sit from the curve, in iRT units, mzLib's robust residual SD with wrong anchors set aside (divide by the curve's slope, iRT per minute, to read it in minutes; NA: not fitted); first_anchor_minutes and last_anchor_minutes, the span the map is fitted over, in minutes (NA: not fitted); and error_kind, error_type and error_message, why mzLib refused the group under on_error = "skip" ("usage", "ArgumentException" and mzLib's message), NA when it was fitted. groups[groups$group == name, ] is one group; groups[!is.na(groups$error_kind), ] the groups mzLib refused.

kind is the kind applied, yours or mzLib's default; minimum_anchors (anchors), bandwidth (fraction of anchors), knots (points) and robustness_iterations (iterations) the options applied, yours or mzLib's; on_error as requested. group_count counts the groups sent (groups), fitted_count those mzLib fitted (groups), failed_count those it refused (groups; non-zero only under "skip"), anchor_count the anchors sent (anchors), query_count the queries sent (queries), and row_count the rows of records (rows): anchor_count + query_count. column_names lists the columns. caveats says what a calibration can and cannot tell you, plus any that apply to this call (queries outside the anchors, groups not fitted).

The traps

iRT is the scale of one library. A calibration maps one run onto the scale of the library the anchors' iRT values came from, so iRT from two libraries is not comparable. **residual_sd is robust**: it understates the spread when many anchors are wrong, and a LOWESS fit to few anchors can pass through nearly all of them, so a residual_sd near 0 there means an overfit, not a perfect run. With few anchors, prefer kind = "linear". Outside the first and last anchor the map is a straight line, not a fit: read is_extrapolated before trusting a converted time there.

Wraps

Wire verb library calibrate-rt. Generated from the bridge's verb spec library.calibrate-rt.yaml (bridge commit 84c3b984b6b9) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

anchors (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 anchor line; optionally a '--' line and query lines. Two lists of tab-separated lines, group, rt_minutes, irt, split by one line holding only '–' (BULK.md section 2). No header; blank lines are skipped; a UTF-8 BOM is dropped. ANCHORS come first: one (observed retention time in minutes, library iRT) pair per line; mzLib asks for the observed apex time of confidently identified precursors (IrtCalibration.cs:29-31), and which ones is the caller's choice. A blank, NA or NaN anchor value reaches mzLib as NaN, which it refuses. QUERIES follow the '–', if any: each gives exactly one of rt_minutes (convert to iRT, IrtCalibrationModel.ToIrt) or irt (convert to minutes, ToRtMinutes) and leaves the other blank. group is any non-empty name, typically the run; each group is fitted by its own IrtCalibration.Fit call on its own anchors, and its queries are converted by that fit. Groups are reported in order of first appearance, over both lists.

kind

string; default lowess; range linear | lowess. IrtCalibrationOptions.Kind. lowess (mzLib's default) is a robust locally weighted regression for a gradient that bends; linear is one straight line, fitted robustly. Absent sends nothing, so mzLib's default applies.

minimum_anchors (wire --minimum-anchors)

int; in anchors; default 20; range >= 3 (mzLib's own check). IrtCalibrationOptions.MinimumAnchors: a group with fewer anchors is refused rather than fitted. Absent means mzLib's default, 20 at the pin; the bridge sends no number of its own.

bandwidth

float; in fraction of anchors; default 0.3; range (0, 1] (mzLib's own check). IrtCalibrationOptions.Bandwidth, LOWESS only: the share of a group's anchors in each local fit (at least 3). Smaller follows the gradient more closely and noise too. Absent means mzLib's default, 0.3 at the pin. mzLib checks it for linear too, and does not use it there.

knots

int; in points; default 100; range >= 3 (mzLib's own check). IrtCalibrationOptions.Knots, LOWESS only: how many evenly spaced times between the first and last anchor the curve is fitted at; between them it is a straight line. Absent means mzLib's default, 100 at the pin.

robustness_iterations (wire --robustness-iterations)

int; in iterations; default 3; range >= 0 (mzLib's own check). IrtCalibrationOptions.RobustnessIterations: rounds of Tukey bisquare reweighting after the first fit, each downweighting anchors with large residuals. 0 keeps the first fit, which is already weighted from binned medians. Absent means mzLib's default, 3 at the pin.

on_error (wire --on-error)

string; default fail; range fail | skip. fail: the first group mzLib refuses (too few anchors, a non-finite one, anchors at one time only, or iRT that does not increase with time) stops the call with a usage error naming the group. skip: that group's error is set, its rows carry the times given and null for the rest, and the other groups are fitted. An option mzLib refuses fails the call either way.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

kind

string; never NA. linear or lowess: the kind applied, as given or mzLib's default.

minimum_anchors

int; in anchors; never NA. The MinimumAnchors applied: as given, or mzLib's default.

bandwidth

float; in fraction of anchors; never NA. The Bandwidth applied: as given, or mzLib's default.

knots

int; in points; never NA. The Knots applied: as given, or mzLib's default.

robustness_iterations

int; in iterations; never NA. The RobustnessIterations applied: as given, or mzLib's default.

on_error

string; never NA. fail or skip, as requested.

group_count

int; in groups; never NA. Distinct groups over both lists.

fitted_count

int; in groups; never NA. Groups mzLib fitted.

failed_count

int; in groups; never NA. Groups mzLib refused; non-zero only under on-error skip.

anchor_count

int; in anchors; never NA. Anchor lines, over every group.

query_count

int; in queries; never NA. Query lines, over every group.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Rows in columns: anchor_count + query_count.

groups

object[]; never NA. One per group in order of first appearance: {group; kind (linear or lowess, IrtCalibrationModel.Kind; null if not fitted); anchor_count (anchors, IrtCalibrationModel.AnchorCount, or the lines sent if not fitted); query_count (queries); residual_sd (iRT units: mzLib's robust residual SD of the anchors that fit, IrtCalibrationModel.ResidualSd; null if not fitted); first_anchor_minutes and last_anchor_minutes (min: the span the map is fitted over, FirstAnchor and LastAnchor; null if not fitted); error ({kind: usage, type: the mzLib exception name, message: mzLib's message} under on-error skip, else null)}.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per stdin line, in input order: the anchors, then the queries.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Five static caveats, plus one when any query falls outside its group's anchors (with the count), and one when any group was not fitted.

Columns of records

group

string; never NA. As given on stdin.

role

string; never NA. anchor; to_irt (a query that gave rt_minutes); or to_minutes (a query that gave irt).

rt_minutes

float; in min; NA when a to_minutes query in a group that was not fitted, or an anchor sent blank or NA in one (mzLib refused it). Retention time in this run: as given for an anchor or a to_irt query; IrtCalibrationModel.ToRtMinutes(irt) for a to_minutes query.

irt

float; in iRT; NA when a to_irt query in a group that was not fitted, or an anchor sent blank or NA in one (mzLib refused it). Indexed retention time on the anchors' library scale: as given for an anchor or a to_minutes query; IrtCalibrationModel.ToIrt(rt_minutes) for a to_irt query.

fitted_irt

float; in iRT; NA when a query, whose irt is itself the converted value, or a group that was not fitted. Anchors only: the fitted map's iRT at the anchor's time, IrtCalibrationModel.ToIrt(rt_minutes). irt minus fitted_irt is the anchor's residual.

is_extrapolated

bool; NA when the group was not fitted. IrtCalibrationModel.IsExtrapolated(rt_minutes): the time lies before the group's first anchor or after its last, where the map is a straight-line continuation rather than a fit.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

kind given without a value or not linear or lowess; minimum-anchors, knots or robustness-iterations not an integer; bandwidth not a number; any of them given without a value; on-error not fail or skip

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

stdin has no anchor line; a line with other than 3 tab-separated fields; an empty group; a value that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN); a second '–' line; a query with both rt_minutes and irt, or with neither; a query value that is not finite

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses an option (IrtCalibrationOptions out of range: MinimumAnchors below 3, Bandwidth outside (0, 1], Knots below 3, RobustnessIterations below 0; mzLib's ArgumentOutOfRangeException, reclassified), whatever on-error says

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

with on-error fail, mzLib refuses a group's anchors: fewer than minimum_anchors (a group with queries and no anchors included), a non-finite value, all at one time, or a fit whose iRT does not increase with time (mzLib's ArgumentException, reclassified); the message starts with the group

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • iRT is the scale of the library the anchors' iRT values came from. A calibration maps one run onto that library's scale, so iRT values from two libraries are not comparable, and the same run calibrated against two libraries gives two maps.

  • The anchors are the caller's choice: mzLib asks for the observed apex retention time, in minutes, of confidently identified precursors paired with their library iRT (IrtCalibration.cs:29-31). The bridge applies no q-value cutoff and removes no duplicate. The fit is robust to some wrong anchors (binned medians, then Tukey bisquare reweighting), not to a wrong choice of them.

  • residual_sd is mzLib's robust residual SD, in iRT units, of the anchors that fit: residuals beyond 3 robust SDs are set aside before it is computed (IrtCalibration.InlierSd). It understates the spread when many anchors are wrong, and a LOWESS fit to few anchors can pass through nearly all of them, so a residual_sd near 0 there means an overfit, not a perfect run. irt minus fitted_irt on the anchor rows shows every residual.

  • Outside each group's first and last anchor the map continues as a straight line, not a fit (IrtCalibrationModel.IsExtrapolated). Read is_extrapolated before trusting a converted time there.

  • The fitted curve itself does not cross the wire: mzLib keeps its knots private and its constructor internal (IrtCalibrationModel), so a calibration cannot be returned and reused. Send the queries in the same call as their anchors; refitting the same anchors gives the same map, because mzLib sorts them first.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.library.calibrate_rt

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::library::calibrate_rt with RtCalibrationOptions

  • R (mzLibR): library_calibrate_rt

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.7.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • The fitted curve cannot be returned: IrtCalibrationModel's knots and end slopes are private fields and its constructor is internal (IrtCalibration.cs:273-278). A public read-only Knots (and the two end slopes) would let the envelope carry each group's curve, at most Knots points, for plotting and for reuse without refitting (PUSH-TO-MAINLAND).

  • IrtCalibration.Line, the two-point line a search uses before any anchors exist, is not projected: it is useful only inside a search engine. Revisit on demand.

  • Calibrated minutes cannot be written back into a .msl: MslLibrary.WithCalibratedRetentionTimes takes a slope and intercept, and mzLib does not route it through IrtCalibrationModel (mzLib #1387 says that is a separate PR).

References

  • doi:10.1002/pmic.201100463: the iRT concept: a normalized, run-independent retention time scale that a run is mapped onto by a calibration (Escher et al., Proteomics 12:1111, 2012)

  • doi:10.1080/01621459.1979.10481038: robust LOWESS with tricube local lines and bisquare reweighting at 6 x the median absolute residual, the curve IrtCalibrationKind.Lowess fits (Cleveland, J Am Stat Assoc 74:829, 1979)

See also

library_read for a library's iRT values, readers_read_records for a search's observed retention times

Examples


# Three 24-minute DIA runs of PBMCs, from a DIA-NN report in mzLib's test data. One precursor,
# AAAAAAAAGAFAGR at charge 2, is held out of the anchors, and each run predicts where it should
# elute from its library iRT:
pbmc <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "calibration", "diann_pbmc_rt.tsv", package = "mzLibR"))
held <- pbmc$precursor_id == "AAAAAAAAGAFAGR2"
anchors <- data.frame(group = pbmc$run[!held], rt_minutes = pbmc$retention_time[!held],
                      irt = pbmc$indexed_retention_time[!held])
queries <- data.frame(group = pbmc$run[held], irt = 11.886096)
calibration <- library_calibrate_rt(anchors, queries, kind = "linear", minimum_anchors = 10)
calibration
#> <mzlibr_rt_calibration> linear: 3 of 3 group(s) fitted from 34 anchors, 3 queries converted
#>   20240316_PBMCs_24min_3Th-1_centroid: linear, 13 anchors over 1.23 to 18.74 min, residual SD 4.07 iRT
#>   20240317_PBMCs_24min_3Th-1_centroid: linear, 11 anchors over 1.261 to 18.73 min, residual SD 3.65 iRT
#>   20240315_PBMCs_24min_3Th-1_centroid: linear, 10 anchors over 1.231 to 18.59 min, residual SD 0.67 iRT
predicted <- calibration$records[calibration$records$role == "to_minutes", ]
# Each prediction is within a quarter of a minute of where the precursor was seen:
data.frame(run = substr(predicted$group, 1, 8), predicted = round(predicted$rt_minutes, 2),
           seen = round(pbmc$retention_time[held], 2))
#>        run predicted seen
#> 1 20240316      9.22 9.21
#> 2 20240317      9.45 9.23
#> 3 20240315      9.17 8.94
